briefings.title: AI and Jobs Series: Fixing the Skills Mismatch and Navigating Upskilling's 'Messy Middle'
briefings.tldr: Labor markets face a critical skills mismatch rather than a talent shortage, requiring organizations to pivot away from traditional degree-based hiring toward skills-first practices and lifelong learning models to navigate the AI era.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Labor markets face a critical skills mismatch rather than a talent shortage, requiring organizations to pivot away from traditional degree-based hiring toward skills-first practices and lifelong learning models to navigate the AI era.

## The Skills Mismatch vs. Talent Shortage
* **Systemic Agility Gap:** **Maria Flynn** notes that public workforce and education systems remain built for the past and are not agile enough to keep pace with AI-driven labor market shifts.
* **Skills as the Future Currency:** According to **Maria Flynn**, organizations struggle with matching talent to roles rather than supply itself, making skills the definitive currency of the future workplace.
* **Lifelong Learning Model:** **Maria Flynn** projects that a 10-year horizon with proper investment will shift society away from a traditional "one-and-done" education approach toward a seamless learning-and-earning model.

## Defining and Implementing Quality Jobs
* **Five Essential Dimensions:** **Maria Flynn** highlights the American Job Quality Study framework, which establishes pay and benefits, career advancement, worker agency/voice, safe and respectful experience, and schedule access/control as core metrics.
* **Worker Voice in AI Adoption:** **Maria Flynn** cites data showing over 60% of workers wish they had more say in how AI is deployed, making authentic feedback channels vital for retention and adoption.
* **Scheduling Policies:** **Maria Flynn** notes that only about 25% of workers currently have quality scheduling policies, despite strong correlations between flexible or regular scheduling and high job satisfaction.

## AI Implementation and the "Messy Middle"
* **Rising Skepticism:** **Maria Flynn** highlights findings from a March 2026 Jobs for the Future survey showing that worker sentiment flipped: while the first year of the survey showed people felt AI did more good than harm, that perception reversed.
* **Demographic Disparities:** **Maria Flynn** points to concerning gender gaps in AI usage, noting that women express more skepticism, fear, and lower engagement than men.
* **Equitable Inclusion Strategies:** **Maria Flynn** recommends structured inclusive gateway courses, cohort-based learning, and visible female tech leadership to counter historical STEM inequities.

## Talent Practices and Human Skills
* **Durable Skills:** **Maria Flynn** emphasizes that human skills like communication, problem-solving, and teamwork remain foundational, drawing a direct line back to the 1990 Secretary's Commission on Achieving Necessary Skills (SCANS).
* **Skills-Based Talent Practices:** **Maria Flynn** advocates moving beyond skills-based hiring to implement skills-first practices across the entire talent lifecycle using platforms like JFF Ventures portfolio company **AdeptID**.
* **Rapid Reskilling vs. Credentials:** **Maria Flynn** states that AI-era reskilling will diverge from post-2008 approaches, focusing on rapid skill acquisition rather than 6-to-18-month credential programs.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Adoption Timeline:** **Maria Flynn** predicts that a four-day work week will not be adopted at scale anytime soon due to the lengthy timelines required for workplace reform to take hold.
* **Expertise Dynamics:** **Maria Flynn** predicts that specialists rather than generalists will hold the advantage in the AI era, as AI democratizes baseline information and makes specialized skills the primary differentiator.
* **The Future of Degrees:** **Maria Flynn** predicts that four-year degrees will remain important but must adapt by embracing experiential learning and embedded career navigation.
* **Resolving the Mismatch:** **Maria Flynn** predicts that the rapid advancement of AI will ultimately force society to fix the skills mismatch out of sheer operational necessity.

## Notable Quotes
> "The worst case scenario that we want to avoid is having workers who do not have the skills that are needed for the jobs of today and for the future."
> — **Maria Flynn**

> "AI is going to make it easier for everyone to be generalists in some way. I think that baseline information will be more accessible... It's folks who are going to be able to kind of use that baseline of general knowledge and augment that with specialized skills and information and kind of analytics that are going to be kind of the most in demand in the future."
> — **Maria Flynn**

briefings.title: All-Hands at Palantir | Dr. Karp on Sovereign AI
briefings.tldr: Dr. Karp outlined Palantir's strategic push into the Sovereign AI revolution, framing it as a global movement to help enterprises and governments protect their intellectual property and maintain control of their production means.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Dr. Karp outlined Palantir's strategic push into the Sovereign AI revolution, framing it as a global movement to help enterprises and governments protect their intellectual property and maintain control of their production means. Comparing this shift to the foundational launch of Gotham (PG), he emphasized that Palantir's unique business model—getting paid as a direct derivative of customer value creation—fully aligns the company with its clients.

## The Intellectual & Strategic Framework of Sovereign AI
* **Parallel to Gotham (PG):** 
  * Just as Gotham reconciled the contradiction between data protection and anti-terror operations, Sovereign AI addresses the tension between enterprise data ownership and AI adoption.
  * The original PG product was technically and conceptually a decade ahead of what customers initially understood.
* **Evolution of the Palantir Stack:** 
  * Key historical components (Gotham, Ontology, FDEs, Foundry, AIP, Maven, Gaia, and Apollo) have built the intellectual groundwork for the current shift.
  * The technical challenge now requires moving Ontology north toward actual fine-tuning and ensuring the full stack works seamlessly with partners like Nvidia.
* **The Global Movement:** 
  * Sovereign AI represents an expansion from intelligence services to the GDP of the US and international allies.
  * Palantir's positioning relies on educating the market about its own interests against external third-party risks.

## Enterprise Frustrations & The AI Lab Backlash
* **Token Slop vs. Business Value:** 
  * Enterprises are increasingly questioning why they pay for tokens that generate low-value output ("slop") while migrating their core business value to external labs.
* **IP and Alpha Migration:** 
  * Customers are frustrated that foundation labs build models by ripping off intellectual property and competing directly against the enterprises that generated the alpha.
* **Wealth Tax Collateral Damage:** 
  * Karp noted broader societal friction, including upcoming wealth taxes affecting the nearly rich and index funds, which clients are sensitive to amid broader economic shifts.

## Alignment & Business Model Differentiation
* **Value-Derivative Pricing:** 
  * Palantir remains unique at scale by getting paid strictly as a derivative of value creation for its customers.
* **Absorbing Risk vs. Outsourcing:** 
  * Unlike competitors who outsource the risk of failure to clients because their tech stacks are bound to fail, Palantir absorbs execution risk through business intuition and forward deployed engineers (FDEs).
* **Maintaining the Means of Production:** 
  * The core message to the market and internal teams is clear: Palantir builds a stack where clients retain the means of their own production.

## Organizational Focus & Execution
* **Internal Reorientation:** 
  * The company is restructuring recruitment, commercial teams, government operations, and partnership decisions around the Sovereign AI revolution.
* **Geographic Reality:** 
  * While Karp emphasized his personal pro-European stance, he acknowledged that the core revolution is currently happening in America and must be captured decisively there first.
* **Propaganda and Messaging:** 
  * Palantir is deploying specialized internal teams (including the authors of the sovereignty document) to shape the narrative around data sovereignty and enterprise alignment.

## Notable Quotes
> "They all sense, every single one, why was I paying why am I paying for tokens that lead to this weird kind of slop that only make the least productive people happy and as simultaneously, migrate the value of my business to a third party?"
> — Dr. Karp

> "The way to answer every question is, 'We are building an we are building a stack where you will maintain the means of your own production.' You own the means of production, we participate because you succeed."
> — Dr. Karp

> "As flawed as we are every day of the week and two times on Wednesday, there is no other institution that's going to do this. And that is a 100% true and it's not because we're so perfect, it's because we built this thing that is just very aligned with this."
> — Dr. Karp

briefings.title: Architecting the Agentic Enterprise | Traversal, Kong, Pigment & Twelve Labs | RAISE 2026
briefings.tldr: While the initial phase of enterprise AI focused on proof-of-concept demos, 2026 demands reliable production deployment, shifting the focus toward robust governance, traceability, deterministic guardrails, and managing enterprise token costs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
While the initial phase of enterprise AI focused on proof-of-concept demos, 2026 demands reliable production deployment, shifting the focus toward robust governance, traceability, deterministic guardrails, and managing enterprise token costs.

## Panelists & Setting
*   **Moderator:** Cathy Gao (Sapphire Ventures)
*   **Carl Mattsson:** Kong Inc. (AI Connectivity)
*   **Eleonore Crespo:** Pigment (AI Business Planning)
*   **Soyoung Lee:** Twelve Labs (Multimodal Video Understanding Models & Agents)
*   **Shubho Sengupta:** Axiom Math (Mathematical Super Intelligence)
*   **Anish Agarwal:** Traversal (Agentic SRE)
*   **Event Context:** Recorded live on the Ada Lovelace Stage at the Carrousel du Louvre, Paris, on July 8, 2026, as part of RAISE Summit 2026.

## POC-to-Production Pitfalls & Governance
*   **Auditability & Trust:** 
    *   **Financial & Regulatory Risk:** High-stress environments like financial services face regulatory scrutiny, requiring agents to be easily auditable and deterministic where possible.
    *   **Autonomous Actions:** As agents move from recommendations to taking direct actions (e.g., healing broken enterprise systems), security teams demand proof that actions won't crash systems.
*   **Traceability Challenges:** Unlike traditional software that fails loudly with a 500 error code, agents fail quietly with incorrect outcomes (akin to a 200 error code), making end-to-end traceability of agentic traffic mandatory.
*   **Accountability Dilemma:** Enterprises are stuck on edge cases because CIOs and CTOs remain unclear on who is legally and operationally accountable when an agent (e.g., granting a loan outside risk profiles) makes a core business error.

## Technical Architecture & Data Layers
*   **Deterministic Layers:** 
    *   **Code and Math:** Shubho Sengupta and Anish Agarwal emphasize that the safest way to ground probabilistic LLMs is to have them output deterministic intermediate steps like code or math before interacting with production systems.
    *   **Multimodal Complexity:** Soyoung Lee notes that video data is inherently undeterministic (combining sound, visuals, time, and narrative), requiring automated compliance and technical defect-checking before human review.
*   **Defensible Moats Beyond the Harness:** 
    *   **Proprietary Data Infrastructure:** Anish Agarwal warns that companies building solely at the harness/API level risk having their work absorbed by frontier model weights. Lasting moats require rebuilding underlying data structures, indexing, and caching to support parallel agent queries.
    *   **Formalized Knowledge:** Axiom Math focuses on building massive indexes of formalized mathematical knowledge to serve as an uncopyable structural foundation.

## Human-in-the-Loop & Organizational Roles
*   **Two-Lens Approach to Automation:** Eleonore Crespo advises dividing workflows into low-risk tasks (where human-in-the-loop can be entirely removed and audited via logs) versus strategic tasks (e.g., hiring plans, budget allocations) that require human checkpoints and context.
*   **Human Bottlenecks and Fatigue:** Carl Mattsson warns that relying on humans to manually review 100% of agent actions fails because human monitors get distracted or bored; systems must intelligently flag only the crucial 1% to 5% of anomalies.
*   **Organizational Shift:** While short-term transformation roles are emerging to accelerate AI adoption, panelists predict these roles will disappear within 3 to 5 years as end users and business functions naturally become "agent managers."

## Pricing, ROI, and Token Management
*   **The ROI Reality Check:** Panelists highlight massive enterprise spend juxtaposed against slow bottom-line (EBITDA) returns, citing examples like Uber burning $3.4 billion on AI spend in a single quarter without clear value capture.
*   **Evolving Pricing Models:**
    *   **Outcome & Consumption Splits:** Eleonore Crespo notes that Pigment prices based on productivity gains and decision quality, while offering a free token-management app paired with Fireworks AI for open-weight model flexibility.
    *   **Predictable and Seat-Based Options:** Soyoung Lee predicts a movement toward fixed, baseline pricing for standard predictable outcomes, with consumption added for extra work.
    *   **AWS-Style Commitments:** Carl Mattsson predicts enterprise pricing will consolidate around large upfront utility commitments drawn down across multiple use cases.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
*   "40% of all the AI initiatives started today or in the last six months is going to die in 2027 because they don't get any business value from what they're actually performing or doing." — Carl Mattsson (citing Gartner stats)
*   "Token cost... will go down in the next couple of years to electricity plus a little bit more." — Carl Mattsson
*   "Everybody, thanks to all of what you said... it will be end-to-end workflows that anybody can run, anyone can become an agent manager... in three to five years max." — Eleonore Crespo

## Notable Quotes
> "The more relevant question to be asking today in 2026 is, not if agents can do anything useful, but can they do anything useful reliably within an enterprise setting?"
> — Cathy Gao

> "Kong is quite fortunate, we work on both sides of the aspect... The enterprises I talk to, specifically the CIO, the CTOs, one of their main issues isn't just technology, governance, how to actually do it... Who is accountable for what the agent does? This is something that comes up a lot."
> — Carl Mattsson

> "If all of the innovation a company is doing is at the harness level, then I think you're, you're going to be in trouble... In my opinion, it's when you have to fundamentally change the data infrastructure level as well."
> — Anish Agarwal

briefings.title: Build for the Memo, Not the Demo — Shawn Chan, China Resources Holdings
briefings.tldr: AI finance products are built to impress for five minutes as demos, but must survive the rigorous scrutiny of investment memos where trust is fragile and unsupported claims carry massive financial risks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI finance products are built to impress for five minutes as demos, but must survive the rigorous scrutiny of investment memos where trust is fragile and unsupported claims carry massive financial risks. Building products and pitches that survive this scrutiny requires uncompromising source accountability, strict separation of facts and guesses, and automated cross-checking of data.

## 1. Demo vs. Memo: The Core Distinction
* **Definition of a Demo:** **Surface-level presentation:** A single clean document in, one fluent answer out, designed to make a room go "oh" for five minutes.
* **Definition of a Memo:** **Survival under scrutiny:** A real committee document built from hundreds of pages, filings, transcripts, and broker notes whose entire job is to survive an aggressive argument.
* **The Cost of Flawed Demos:** **The $100 Billion Typo:** In February 2023, a major tech company launched an AI assistant with a promotional demo that provided a wrong fact about a space telescope, causing the stock to drop roughly 8% in a day (about $100 billion in value) due to an unchecked marketing sentence.

## 2. Six Ways Trust Quietly Breaks in AI Systems
* **Source Quality Neglect:** **Audits vs. rumors:** Most retrieval systems treat numbers from an audited filing (accountant under oath) the exact same as a rough guess from a group chat text from six months earlier.
* **Internal Numerical Inconsistencies:** **Unchecked math:** A memo stating 18% growth on page 1 and 17.4% on page 11 signals a lack of basic verification.
  * *Real Estate Warning:* A major American real estate company let an algorithm buy houses at scale based on overly confident house prices, resulting in writing off around half a billion dollars, shutting the unit down, and laying off a quarter of the staff.
* **Smooth Contradiction Smoothing:** **Hiding disagreements:** AI systems are trained to be smooth and helpful, automatically picking the nicer version when sources conflict instead of flagging the vital gap between a CEO earnings call and an official filing.
* **Melting Facts and Guesses:** **Fact-shaped estimates:** Statements like "the company will likely get approval next quarter" start as guesses but wear fact costumes across drafts until they are treated as proven receipts.
* **Hallucinated Citations:** **The invisible source:** A New York lawyer filed a brief with AI-generated court cases that did not exist; when asked if they were real, the chatbot confidently said yes, resulting in a judge's fine.
* **Absence of Human Accountability:** **The chatbot excuse:** An airline chatbot promised a grieving customer a bereavement discount policy that did not exist, leading the airline to argue in a tribunal that the chatbot was a separate legal entity responsible for its own actions.

## 3. The Five-Point Vendor and Product Fix
* **Every Claim Needs a Receipt:** **Direct source linking:** Each sentence must link straight to its source paragraph with the source trust level attached, rather than a generic citation tab at the end.
* **Visible Separation of Facts and Guesses:** **Distinct categorization:** A single glance at the page must instantly reveal what is proven versus what is someone's best estimate.
* **Automatic Numerical Agreement:** **Enforced consistency:** The system must refuse to generate a memo where figures do not match across pages, removing the need for manual 2:00 AM human checks.
* **Surface Contradictions:** **Raising a hand:** When sources disagree, the system must highlight the conflict instead of smoothing it over with a default answer.
* **Locked Human Approval Gates:** **Auditable sign-offs:** Every decision requires a logged human approval gate detailing who reviewed it, what changed, and when they signed.

briefings.title: Coinbase Q2 2026 Earnings AMA w/ Brian Armstrong & Alesia Haas
briefings.tldr: Coinbase reported a diversified revenue base where Bitcoin-related transactions now comprise 12% of total revenue, while advancing multi-chain strategies, Base ecosystem growth, and AI-agent financial infrastructure.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Coinbase reported a diversified revenue base where Bitcoin-related transactions now comprise 12% of total revenue, while advancing multi-chain strategies, Base ecosystem growth, and AI-agent financial infrastructure.

## Regulatory Landscape & Clarity Act
* **Legislative Outlook:** CEO Brian Armstrong expressed optimism that the Clarity Act will reach a full Senate floor vote before the August recess, citing thousands of hours of Senate staff work and high advocacy engagement.
* **Stand With Crypto Impact:** Highlighted over one million emails and phone calls sent by advocates to their representatives.
* **Contingency Plan:** If the legislation fails, Armstrong stated it is "business as usual" because Coinbase already operates under high compliance best practices, and agency heads Chair Atkins (SEC) and Celeg (CFTC) have signaled intentions to pass clear rules regardless.

## Stablecoin Strategy & The Circle Partnership
* **Circle Contract Renewal:** CFO Alesia Haas confirmed that Coinbase has met all conditions for the Circle contract to renew on the same terms, removing market ambiguity regarding USDC.
* **Multi-Stablecoin Platform:** Armstrong explained that Coinbase supports competing options like PayPal PYUSD and USDT, and participates in the OpenUSD (OUSD) consortium to capture additional business, FX trading, and revenue opportunities.
* **Hyperliquid Integration:** Haas and Armstrong defended sharing economics with Hyperliquid to deeply embed USDC in an active market-maker ecosystem, driving network effects to challenge Tether's market cap leadership.

## Base Ecosystem & Competitive Dynamics
* **Base Metrics & Adoption:** Base achieved $32 trillion in stablecoin transfer volume over the preceding 12 months, serves as the leading L2 on Ethereum, and captures the majority of agentic finance transactions using Explorer 2.
* **Competitor L2s:** Comparing recent competitor chains launched by Stripe and Robinhood to past stablecoin proliferation, Armstrong expects an eventual consolidation and M&A phase in the blockchain market, noting Coinbase maintains a roughly two-year head start.

## Product Velocity & Coinbase One Growth
* **Subscriber Milestones:** Haas announced an all-time high in paid Coinbase One subscribers during Q2 2026 despite down crypto trading volumes.
* **Unit Economics & Engagement:** Coinbase One members demonstrate higher retention rates, trade more frequently, use multiple products (such as staking and the Coinbase One card), and yield accretive overall unit economics despite zero-fee trading tiers.
* **Growth Marketing:** Marketing efforts currently target prediction markets and crypto derivatives, achieving a payback period outperforming the one-year benchmark and driving incremental spot trading volume without cannibalization.

## Revenue Diversification & Emerging Verticals
* **Reduced Bitcoin Concentration:** Bitcoin-related transactions dropped from over 50% of company revenue historically down to 12% in Q2 2026.
* **Pre-IPO Perpetual Futures:** Non-US traders gained access to private company perps starting with SpaceX; Armstrong confirmed US approval is actively on the roadmap.
* **Agentic Finance & AI Agents:** Armstrong noted that AI agents prioritize low cost, speed (sub-second settlement on Base), reliability, and liquidity, making Coinbase's trust moat critical for autonomous transactions.

## Leadership Transitions
* **Succession Planning:** Armstrong and Haas addressed senior leadership departures this quarter, emphasizing a deep internal talent bench and smooth transitions for incoming leaders like Dominique (People), Molly (Legal), and Liz.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Regulatory Rulemaking:** If the Clarity Act fails, SEC Chair Atkins and CFTC Chair Celeg will come out with their own rules allowing businesses like Coinbase to continue operating with more clarity — Brian Armstrong.
* **Blockchain Consolidation:** The market will transition from current fragmentation to a consolidation and M&A phase similar to historical patterns in automobiles, trains, and stablecoins — Brian Armstrong.
* **US Pre-IPO Access:** Coinbase will continue pushing for regulatory approval to offer pre-IPO perpetual futures to US customers — Brian Armstrong.

## Notable Quotes
> "The American consumers, as you mentioned, who would lose if Clarity doesn't pass. I think Coinbase would be fine."
> — Brian Armstrong

> "We have already met the conditions for the Circle contract to renew. So, it will renew on the same terms. I want to take away any ambiguity about that for the market."
> — Alesia Haas

> "When customers store with us, they transact with us. So, then when we get to our growth marketing strategy, it really looks to what product is meeting the market need and where do we see activity coming from in our retail customer base."
> — Alesia Haas

briefings.title: How Lassie Is Automating Healthcare Administration
briefings.tldr: Lassie co-founders Steijn Pelle and Frédéric Renken, joined by a16z's Alex Rampell and Olivia Moore, discuss how Lassie's AI agents automate administrative work—such as insurance claims, billing, and payments—for small healthcare businesses, freeing dental practices from overwhelming paperwork amid a severe labor shortage.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Lassie co-founders Steijn Pelle and Frédéric Renken, joined by a16z's Alex Rampell and Olivia Moore, discuss how Lassie's AI agents automate administrative work—such as insurance claims, billing, and payments—for small healthcare businesses, freeing dental practices from overwhelming paperwork amid a severe labor shortage.

## The Dental Practice Administrative Crisis
* **Severe Administrative Burden:** 
  * Small business owners like dentists spend roughly 200 hours a month on paperwork and busywork by hand (e.g., submitting insurance claims, billing patients).
  * Administrative costs run about $200,000 per year across the roughly 160,000 dental practices in the US.
* **The Labor Shortage Driver:** 
  * Practices cannot find staff ("Betty quit two weeks ago"), forcing doctors with advanced degrees to work until midnight on bookkeeping or take early retirement out of frustration.
  * The software industry previously only digitized filing cabinets (storing data in databases via on-prem or green screens) rather than performing the actual work of labor.

## Building and Scaling Autonomous AI Agents
* **From Humans-in-the-Loop to Autonomy:** 
  * The founders initially acted as the human-in-the-loop, doing the billing and finances themselves inside real dental practices (such as Dr. Quan's office and Dr. Shah's office in Scranton, PA) to automate away their own problems.
  * Lassie’s agents achieve roughly **98% automation**, leaving a tiny sliver of edge cases handled with input from thousands of office staffers.
* **Technical Complexity and Defensibility:** 
  * Building a reliable agent required creating read-and-write integrations across fragmented systems and establishing a unified data model/ontology for insurance claims and patient payments.
  * Because many small business categories lack incumbent software solutions, and because incumbents struggle with nimble innovation, this deep operational "schlepp" creates strong defensibility.

## Main Street Distribution and Onboarding
* **Overcoming the Iowa Distribution Problem:** 
  * AI is underhyped in Iowa compared to Silicon Valley; reaching busy, non-technical owners like Dr. Sloop requires going beyond typical B2B tech playbooks (as these owners are rarely on LinkedIn or Apollo).
  * Lassie leverages consumer-grade product backgrounds (from Robinhood and Superhuman) to build a self-serve onboarding flow—similar to Stripe or Reppling—where users hook up bank accounts, system of records, and insurance portals in minutes.
* **The Payment Digitization Tailwind:** 
  * Approximately 70% of small businesses still receive paper checks and itemized invoices, requiring manual opening and physical bank deposits.
  * Federal regulatory mandates shifting the industry toward direct digital deposits and digital file formats provide a massive tailwind for software adoption.

## Master Plan and Future Vision
* **Vertical Expansion Strategy:** 
  * **Step 1:** Dominate the 160,000 US dental practices representing a $1 billion recurring revenue market.
  * **Step 2:** Expand into another underserved doctor office type that requires consumer-grade onboarding and high automation accuracy.
  * **Step 3:** Scale AI agents across all small businesses globally so every business can run itself autonomously, interfacing between business agents, consumer personal agents, and insurance agents.

## Notable Quotes
> "The number one rated doctor on Yelp, spending 200 hours a month on paperwork... This is a real problem they have. This is not some vitamin... this is something that keeps them up at night. It makes them almost quit their job."
> — **Steijn Pelle**

> "It's not like, oh, AI is going to take the jobs. In many cases, you can't find somebody... The incumbent was named Betty, and she quit two weeks ago. That's the incumbent."
> — **Alex Rampell**

> "We are literally digitizing the file cabinet... Dr. Sloot needs to also then spend 50 hours figuring out with Signa and Delta and all the other insurance companies, 'How do I flip the switch?'"
> — **Steijn Pelle**

briefings.title: Jeff Dean: The 1% Rule for Building in AI
briefings.tldr: Google Chief Scientist Jeff Dean and YC’s Diana Hu discuss AI progress, hardware breakthroughs, inference scaling, and why small teams can win by focusing on context engineering and niche problem domains.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Google Chief Scientist Jeff Dean and YC’s Diana Hu discuss AI progress, hardware breakthroughs, inference scaling, and why small teams can win by focusing on context engineering and niche problem domains.

## The State of AI & Junior Engineers
- **Agent-Based Coding Capability:** Models are now performing well on longer-running, agent-based coding tasks, effectively operating at the level of a junior engineer.
- **Underestimated Rate of Progress:** Complex task execution and agent application outside of coding have accelerated faster than initially predicted.
- **2027 Outlook — Automated ML Improvements:** Future systems will feature fully automated problem decomposition and experimentation loops, allowing ML systems (and other scientific fields) to continuously improve their own capabilities against measurable objectives.

## Hardware, Energy, and the "Inference Moment"
- **The 2001 Search Analogy:** In 2001, Jeff Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat realized Google's search index fit in RAM and shipped a RAM-based search version in days. The 2026 equivalent is high-performance, low-energy **inference hardware** that drastically cuts latency (e.g., 50x better).
- **The TPU Origin Story (2013 Napkin Math):** 
  - Realizing that 3 minutes of daily voice recognition per Google user would double the server fleet, Dean and Sanjay built the TPU—specialized for low-precision dense linear algebra.
  - The resulting chip was **30 to 80 times more energy-efficient** and **20 to 30 times lower latency** than contemporary CPUs and GPUs.
- **The Data Movement Energy Gap:** Moving data from accelerator memory (HBM) to the processor costs **1,000x more energy** than performing the actual computation. This hardware reality dictates why batching is necessary.

## Context Engineering & Long-Running Agents
- **Context vs. Training Data:** The model is only one piece of an overall system. Context engineering (retrieval, tool use, memory) provides clear information directly to the model, unlike trillions of training tokens stirred into a parameter soup.
- **Long-Running Agents:** Agents can now run for days or weeks on complex tasks (e.g., rewriting software in a new programming language for better safety or performance).
- **Overcoming Agent Rail Failures:** 
  - Multi-agent systems use inference-time compute to search through multiple potential solutions and evaluate the most promising paths.
  - Providing explicit guidelines, skills, and performance hints (such as Dean and Sanjay's published 30-page "Performance Hints" document) helps keep models on successful execution paths.

## Startup Opportunities & Where 2-3 People Can Win
- **Targeting 0% Success Rates:** Founders should look for problems where current general models succeed 0% to 1% of the time, rather than 20% (which indicates general capabilities are rapidly encroaching).
- **Privileged Data & Niche Models:** 
  - Build around personal/private data that general models cannot access.
  - Build specialized niche models (similar to AlphaFold for protein folding) for domains like material science or chip design.
- **The Power of Good Taste:** As AI automates code writing, the scarce, high-value skill is having great taste and wisdom regarding *what* problem to work on.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Jeff Dean (2027 Outlook):** ML systems will extensively automate their own capability improvements by running large-scale automated experimentation loops by 2027.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Imagine what you could do with something where the latency is, you know, 50x better."*
> — **Jeff Dean**

> *"If you truly understand the data, you should be able to compress it really well."*
> — **Jeff Dean**

> *"Look for something where the model succeeds 0% or 1% of the time, not 20%."*
> — **Jeff Dean**
